reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is converting high-dimensional spatio-temporal video data into precise event timestamps while maintaining robustness to environmental variations. We achieve this by first applying a keypoint transformer that compresses per-frame entity observations into a fixed-size latent representation, effectively filtering noise and focusing on discriminative features. This condensed representation is then fed into a temporal transformer which estimates the discrete time-to-event distances. The dual-time formulation (next vs. previous event) naturally handles the sequential nature of table tennis matches where events alternate. Crucially, our 3D reprojection augmentation explicitly enforces geometric consistency across viewpoints, preventing overfitting to camera angles present in training data. The ablation study reveals that the temporal transformer contributes most to precision, while the keypoint condensation stabilizes recall by reducing false positives from background clutter. This modular design allows straightforward integration of additional modalities such as audio or physics-based constraints.
